html:
A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was the engineer who led India's rocket and missile projects and then served as president from 2002 to 2007. He was one of the best loved public figures in the country.

He was born in 1931 at Rameswaram, an island pilgrim town in Tamil Nadu, into a poor Tamil Muslim family that hired out boats. As a boy he delivered newspapers. He studied aircraft engineering in Madras and narrowly missed becoming a pilot.

At the space agency (see ISRO) he led the team that built India's first satellite launcher. It failed in 1979 and worked in July 1980. He then moved to defence research and from 1983 ran the programme that produced the Prithvi and Agni missiles, which earned him the name Missile Man. He was a chief organiser of the nuclear tests of 1998.

In 2002 the ruling BJP and the opposition Congress both backed him for president. He opened the palace to the public and answered children's letters himself. His memoir Wings of Fire sold more than a million copies.

He lived simply, never married, and owned little but books and a veena. He died in 2015 after collapsing while giving a lecture to students in Shillong.
sum: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was the engineer who led India's rocket and missile projects and then served as president from 2002 to 2007. He was one of the best loved public figures in the country.
